facts.text: Queen Street, named for Queen Victoria, hosts Brisbane's largest pedestrian mall, Queen Street Mall.

Streets parallel to Queen Street honor female royalty—Adelaide, Alice, Ann, Charlotte, Elizabeth, Margaret, and Mary—while perpendicular streets honor male royalty—Albert, Edward, George, and William.
The CBD sits on the northern bank of the Brisbane River, historically called Meanjin in the local Yuggera dialect.
Before becoming the city centre, the area was known as Petrie Gardens, an early settlement farm that supplied food to the colony.
The CBD’s triangular peninsula, known at its tip as Gardens Point, slopes upward to the northwest toward the inner‑city suburb of Spring Hill.
Bus services centre on Queen Street bus station and King George Square busway station, while trains stop at Central and Roma Street stations.
